<strong>Correlación no implica causalida:
Correlation does not imply causation. Ice cream consumption and drownings are extremely highly correlated, and it is not that ice cream drowns anybody: both depend on a third variable, the heat. This sentence is the most important in the whole statistics block and the one most ignored in the newspapers.

That said, the warning is incomplete if nothing is said about what to do about it, because there is some way of finding out what causes what: doctors prescribe and engineers decide. The last topic of this block, [[pe-causal|Causal inference]], is about exactly that.

El coeficiente de correlación se usa a d: The correlation coefficient is used daily to decide where to put money. An investment fund does not look for the assets that rise most, but for assets that are weakly correlated with each other: if everything you hold rises and falls at once, you have diversified nothing, you have only bought the same thing under different names. The 2008 scare came largely from correlations thought to be small all shooting up at once.

En medicina y en industria sirve para ot: In medicine and in industry it serves another purpose: discarding measurements that are surplus. If two sensors on a machine give readings with correlation 0.99, one of the two is dispensable; if a clinical test correlates almost perfectly with a cheaper one, the cheap one is ordered. La palabra <em>regresión</em> viene de u: The word regression comes from an uncomfortable finding. In 1886 Francis Galton measured the heights of parents and children and discovered that the children of the very tall tended to be somewhat shorter than their parents, and those of the very short somewhat taller: there was a “regression towards the mean”. Galton read it in hereditary and eugenic terms, which today is indefensible, but the phenomenon is real and still explains why the best team of a season almost never repeats the following year.
